source: NCERT-aligned UPSC Ecology & Environment (Class XI), Ch. 2 (Biogeochemical Cycles and Ecological Succession).

sections.heading: 1. Biogeochemical Cycles
points: **Biogeochemical cycles** = the movement of **nutrients** between the living (biotic) and non-living (abiotic) components of the ecosystem.
Two types: **gaseous cycles** (reservoir = atmosphere/hydrosphere — carbon, nitrogen, oxygen) and **sedimentary cycles** (reservoir = earth's crust — phosphorus, sulphur).

sections.heading: 2. Carbon and Nitrogen Cycles
points: **Carbon cycle** — carbon moves via **photosynthesis (fixation), respiration, decomposition and combustion**; burning fossil fuels adds CO₂ (global warming).

**Nitrogen cycle** — atmosphere is ~78% N₂ but unusable directly; **nitrogen fixation** (by bacteria like Rhizobium, lightning) → nitrification → assimilation → ammonification → **denitrification** (returns N₂ to air).
Legumes (with Rhizobium in root nodules) fix nitrogen naturally.

sections.heading: 3. Phosphorus Cycle
points: **Phosphorus cycle** — a **sedimentary** cycle; reservoir = rocks; released by **weathering**, taken up by plants, returned via decomposition.
No significant atmospheric (gaseous) phase; slower than gaseous cycles.
Excess phosphorus/nitrogen (from fertilisers) causes **eutrophication** of water bodies.

sections.heading: 4. Ecological Succession
points: **Ecological succession** = the gradual and orderly change in the species of a community over time, ending in a stable **climax community**.
**Primary succession** — on a bare, lifeless area (bare rock, new island); starts with **pioneer species (lichens)**; very slow.
**Secondary succession** — on a disturbed area that still has soil (after fire/flood); faster.
**Hydrarch** (in water → land) and **xerarch** (in dry areas) successions; end at the **climax** (e.g. forest).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Gaseous cycles (carbon, nitrogen — atmospheric reservoir); sedimentary (phosphorus, sulphur — crust).
Nitrogen fixation by Rhizobium (legume nodules) and lightning; denitrification returns N₂.
Phosphorus cycle = sedimentary (no atmospheric phase).
Succession → climax community; pioneer species = lichens (primary succession).
Primary succession on bare rock (slow); secondary on soil-bearing disturbed land (faster).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Phosphorus cycle is sedimentary** (no gaseous/atmospheric phase).
**Nitrogen fixation** by **Rhizobium** (in legume root nodules); **denitrification** releases N₂.
**Pioneer species in primary succession = lichens**.
**Secondary succession is faster** than primary (soil already present).
